input.quote: 20.1 Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents from each third-party claim and resulting damages, settlements, judgments, penalties, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.
input.rationale: Section 20 meets the preferred position in full, so no redline is proposed. § 20.1 gives an express Vendor duty to defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates against third-party claims that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate IP. § 20.2 extends the same defence and indemnity to Vendor's breach of Applicable Law, unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor, and Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud. § 20.4 supplies the standard procedure (prompt notice, reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense, control of the defence) with a materiality-of-prejudice qualifier and a consent gate on adverse settlements. Customer's reciprocal indemnity in § 20.3 is properly narrow: unmodified Customer-supplied material used strictly as authorized, plus Customer's own violation of Applicable Law, with carve-outs for Vendor Technology, modification, combination and instructions. Two points run better than the fallback and need no action: § 20.5 gives procure / modify-or-replace / terminate-and-refund remedies in addition to (not in substitution for) the defence obligation, and § 21.3 lists indemnification obligations, IP infringement and gross negligence/wilful misconduct as Excluded Claims, so Vendor's indemnity sits outside the § 21.1 cap entirely rather than being confined to a 3x annual-fees super-cap. Worth noting only in passing, not as a deviation: § 20.1 carries no express Customer-modification, combination or specification exclusions, which broadens the IP indemnity in our favour (the fallback treats those exclusions as permitted, not required); and §§ 19.4-19.5 confirm no warranty remedy or disclaimer dilutes the indemnity.
